title: Quick Start
text: simulate two-modality dataset 20 samples (10 per condition), 20% features undergo connectivity rewiring conditions B. returned Seurat objects include ground-truth labels: feature_cluster (module feature belongs ) is_de (whether feature rewired).
code:
library(MOSAIC) library(ggplot2)  sim <- simulate_multimodal_data(   simulation_type = "DC",   n_features = c(500, 400),   signal_prop = 0.2,   seed = 42,   rescale = TRUE,   add_batch = FALSE,   nonlinear = FALSE,   sample_noise_level = 0.5,   feature_noise_level = 0.5,   cell_noise_level = 0.5 )  cat("Modalities:", length(sim$seurat_list), "
") #> Modalities: 2 cat("Samples:", nrow(sim$sample_metadata), "
") #> Samples: 20 cat("Features per modality:", sapply(sim$seurat_list, nrow), "
") #> Features per modality: 500 400 # Ground truth for modality 1 feat_meta <- sim$seurat_list[[1]][["originalexp"]][[]] cat("DC features in modality 1:", sum(feat_meta$is_de), "/", nrow(feat_meta), "
") #> DC features in modality 1: 100 / 500

title: Quick Start
text: Rewired features (is_de) move different module condition B, also changes coupling profiles features coupled . evaluate well pseudo-F statistic ranks rewired features.
code:
# Ground truth: combine is_de from both modalities ground_truth <- c(   sim$seurat_list[[1]][["originalexp"]][[]]$is_de,   sim$seurat_list[[2]][["originalexp"]][[]]$is_de ) true_dc <- which(ground_truth)  # Rank features by the observed pseudo-F statistic hits <- ground_truth[order(-dc$results$F_stat)] average_precision <- sum(cumsum(hits)[hits] / which(hits)) / sum(hits) top_k_precision <- mean(hits[seq_len(sum(hits))])  cat(sprintf("Average precision: %.3f (random ranking: %.2f)
",             average_precision, mean(ground_truth))) #> Average precision: 0.890 (random ranking: 0.20) cat(sprintf("Precision among the top %d features: %.3f
",             sum(hits), top_k_precision)) #> Precision among the top 180 features: 0.783  # Features significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction cat(sum(dc$results$padj < 0.05), "features with BH-adjusted P < 0.05, of which",     sum(dc$results$padj[true_dc] < 0.05), "of", length(true_dc), "rewired features
") #> 357 features with BH-adjusted P < 0.05, of which 172 of 180 rewired features

code: sim_list <- compute_feature_similarity(result$mosaic_embed_list) sim_vectors <- lapply(sim_list, function(mat) {   mat[upper.tri(mat, diag = FALSE)] })  strat_matrix <- do.call(cbind, sim_vectors) feature_corr <- cor(strat_matrix, method = "spearman")

title: Quick Start
code: library(dynamicTreeCut)  dist_feat <- as.dist(1 - feature_corr) hc_feat <- hclust(dist_feat, method = "ward.D2")  feature_clusters <- cutreeDynamic(   dendro = hc_feat,   distM = as.matrix(dist_feat),   minClusterSize = 15,   method = "hybrid",   deepSplit = 2 ) #>  ..cutHeight not given, setting it to 8.38  ===>  99% of the (truncated) height range in dendro. #>  ..done. names(feature_clusters) <- colnames(feature_corr)  module_ids <- sort(unique(feature_clusters[feature_clusters > 0])) cat(length(module_ids), "modules identified\n") #> 26 modules identified cat("Module sizes:", sapply(module_ids, function(m) sum(feature_clusters == m)), "\n") #> Module sizes: 126 107 55 42 41 38 34 32 31 31 30 28 28 27 25 25 25 24 23 21 20 19 19 18 16 15

what: Multi-Omic Sample-Wise Analysis of Inter-Feature Connectivity
title: Multi-Omic Sample-Wise Analysis of Inter-Feature Connectivity
text: MOSAIC (Multi-Omic Sample-wise Analysis Inter-feature Connectivity) spectral framework learns high-resolution feature × sample joint embedding population-scale single-cell multi-omics data. individual, MOSAIC constructs sample-specific coupling matrix capturing intra- cross-modality feature-feature associations, projects samples shared latent space via spectral integration. resulting embedding represents feature connectivity profile, pattern association features, connectivity profiles can compared directly across individuals. MOSAIC supports three downstream applications: Differential Connectivity (DC) Analysis: tests condition-associated shifts shared representation feature’s connectivity profile, using samples units comparison. Unsupervised Subgroup Detection: groups multi-modal features coherent modules tests whether specific modules delineate distinct patient subtypes. Clinical Outcome Prediction: leverages connectivity-derived features complementary signal abundance-based analysis improved disease classification. MOSAIC run cells one annotated population (e.g. one cell type). Documentation: https://klugerlab.github.io/MOSAIC/ Paper analyses: reproducibility/

title: Multi-Omic Sample-Wise Analysis of Inter-Feature Connectivity
code: library(MOSAIC)  # --- Run MOSAIC embedding (cells of one annotated population) ---  # One modality (e.g. RNA only) result <- run_MOSAIC(   list(RNA = seurat_rna),   assays = c("RNA"),   sample_meta = "sample_id",   condition_meta = "condition" )  # Two modalities (e.g. RNA + ATAC) result <- run_MOSAIC(   list(RNA = seurat_rna, ATAC = seurat_atac),   assays = c("RNA", "ATAC"),   sample_meta = "sample_id",   condition_meta = "condition" )  # Three modalities (e.g. RNA + ATAC + ADT) result <- run_MOSAIC(   list(RNA = seurat_rna, ATAC = seurat_atac, ADT = seurat_adt),   assays = c("RNA", "ATAC", "ADT"),   sample_meta = "sample_id",   condition_meta = "condition" )  # --- Differential Connectivity Analysis --- dc <- run_DC_test(result$mosaic_embed_list,                   groups = result$annotation$Condition) head(dc$results[order(dc$results$pvalue, -dc$results$F_stat), ])  # Paired design: permute labels within donor dc <- run_DC_test(result$mosaic_embed_list,                   groups = result$annotation$Condition,                   blocks = donor_ids)  # --- Subgroup Detection --- # Per-feature stratification profiles sim_list <- compute_feature_similarity(result$mosaic_embed_list)  # Module-level sample similarity sim_mat <- compute_module_similarity(   result$mosaic_embed_list,   feature_idx = which(feature_clusters == module_id) )  # Test for balanced partition partition <- find_partition_hclust(as.dist(1 - sim_mat))  # --- Visualization --- plot_eigen(result$eigenvalues)  plot_mds_cluster(   sim_list[[1]],   title = "Feature Embedding",   cluster = result$annotation$Condition )

what: Find the Elbow Point Using the Kneedle Algorithm — find_elbow_kneedle
title: Find the Elbow Point Using the Kneedle Algorithm — find_elbow_kneedle
text: Automatically selects effective dimensionality decreasing eigenvalue sequence. algorithm log-transforms eigenvalues, normalizes axes unit interval, draws straight line first last points, returns index point greatest perpendicular distance line. point corresponds "elbow" eigenvalue decay transitions steep flat. returned index least 2.

title: Find the Elbow Point Using the Kneedle Algorithm — find_elbow_kneedle
code: find_elbow_kneedle(eigenvalues)

title: Find the Elbow Point Using the Kneedle Algorithm — find_elbow_kneedle
text: eigenvalues Numeric vector eigenvalues, typically decreasing order. Non-positive values automatically replaced preceding value ensure valid log transform. Must length >= 3 meaningful result; shorter, full length returned.

title: Find the Elbow Point Using the Kneedle Algorithm — find_elbow_kneedle
text: integer: 1-based index elbow point, least 2 (full length fewer three eigenvalues given). example, return value 5 means first 5 eigenvalues capture dominant signal.

title: Find the Elbow Point Using the Kneedle Algorithm — find_elbow_kneedle
text: MOSAIC calls function internally two stages: (1) choose per-sample rank coupling matrix eigendecomposition, (2) choose global rank aggregated projection.

title: Find the Elbow Point Using the Kneedle Algorithm — find_elbow_kneedle
code: # Typical eigenvalue decay eigenvalues <- c(10, 5, 3, 2, 1.5, 1.2, 1.1, 1.05, 1.01, 1.0) find_elbow_kneedle(eigenvalues) #> [1] 5 # Returns 5  # Visualize the elbow plot(eigenvalues, type = "b", pch = 19, xlab = "Index", ylab = "Eigenvalue") abline(v = find_elbow_kneedle(eigenvalues), col = "red", lty = 2)

text: function used MOSAIC's subgroup detection pipeline test whether feature module defines meaningful patient subtypes: compute module similarity matrix compute_module_similarity, convert distance, test balanced partition .

title: Find a Balanced Two-Way Partition via Hierarchical Clustering — find_partition_hclust
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Compute module similarity sim_mat <- compute_module_similarity(   result$mosaic_embed_list,   feature_idx = which(feature_clusters == module_id) )  # Test for subgroups partition <- find_partition_hclust(as.dist(1 - sim_mat))  if (partition$balanced) {   cat("Silhouette:", partition$silhouette, "\n")   cat("Group sizes:", table(partition$groups), "\n")    # Visualize   plot_mds_cluster(sim_mat, "Subgroups",                    cluster = partition$groups) }  # Permutation test for significance n_perm <- 1000 null_sils <- numeric(n_perm) for (p in seq_len(n_perm)) {   rand_idx <- sample(total_features, length(module_idx))   rand_sim <- compute_module_similarity(projected_list, rand_idx)   rand_part <- find_partition_hclust(as.dist(1 - rand_sim))   null_sils[p] <- ifelse(rand_part$balanced, rand_part$silhouette, 0) } pval <- (sum(null_sils >= partition$silhouette) + 1) / (n_perm + 1) } # }

text: similarity_matrix square numeric matrix pairwise similarities distances. default, treated similarity matrix converted dissimilarity via 1 - x. title: MDS Plot with Cluster Coloring — plot_mds_cluster
code: # Create a toy similarity matrix set.seed(42) sim <- matrix(runif(100, 0.5, 1), 10, 10) sim <- (sim + t(sim)) / 2  # make symmetric diag(sim) <- 1 rownames(sim) <- colnames(sim) <- paste0("S", 1:10) groups <- rep(c("A", "B"), each = 5)  plot_mds_cluster(sim, "Example MDS", cluster = groups) #> Warning: minimal value for n is 3, returning requested palette with 3 different levels   # With custom colors and no ellipses plot_mds_cluster(sim, "Custom Colors", cluster = groups,                  custom_colors = c("A" = "#56B4E9", "B" = "#E69F00"),                  add_ellipse = FALSE, size = 3)   if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Visualize the sample embeddings of a feature (Euclidean distances, as in # the differential connectivity test) M_f <- t(sapply(result$mosaic_embed_list, function(e) e["RNA_STAT5B", ])) plot_mds_cluster(   as.matrix(dist(M_f)), dis = TRUE,   title = "STAT5B",   cluster = paste0("Day_", result$annotation$Condition),   custom_colors = c("Day_0" = "#56B4E9", "Day_7" = "#E69F00") ) } # }

title: Run Differential Connectivity Test — run_DC_test
text: Tests feature condition-associated shift MOSAIC embedding. feature, PERMANOVA pseudo-F statistic computed distances sample embeddings, significance assessed permuting condition labels across samples embedding held fixed. label assignments used features; feature compared null distribution.

title: Run Differential Connectivity Test — run_DC_test
code: run_DC_test(   mosaic_embed_list,   groups,   blocks = NULL,   n_perm = 999,   max_exact = 2e+05,   dist_method = c("euclidean", "cosine"),   seed = NULL,   feature_chunk = 2000,   perm_chunk = 2000,   return_null = FALSE )

title: Run Differential Connectivity Test — run_DC_test
text: mosaic_embed_list Named list per-sample embedding matrices (features x latent dimensions), returned run_MOSAIC()$mosaic_embed_list. matrices must features order. groups Character factor vector condition labels, one per sample, order mosaic_embed_list. blocks Optional vector block labels (e.g. donor IDs), one per sample. given, labels permuted within blocks. Default NULL (samples exchangeable). n_perm Integer. Number random assignments used admissible set large enumerate. Default 999. max_exact Numeric. Enumerate admissible assignments number value. Set 0 always use random assignments. Default 2e5. dist_method Distance sample embeddings feature: "euclidean" (default) "cosine" (\(1 -\) cosine similarity). seed Optional integer seed random assignments. feature_chunk, perm_chunk Integers controlling memory use: number features assignments processed . return_null Logical. TRUE, also return full features x assignments matrix permutation pseudo-F statistics assignment matrix. Default FALSE.

title: Run Differential Connectivity Test — run_DC_test
text: list elements results Data frame one row per feature: feature, F_stat (observed pseudo-F), R2 (\(SS_B / SS_T\)), pvalue padj (Benjamini-Hochberg). exact Logical, whether P-values exact. n_perm Number assignments evaluated (\(|\Pi|\) exact). min_pvalue Smallest attainable P-value. F_null, assignments return_null = TRUE: permutation statistics (features x assignments) assignments (samples x assignments, group labels).

title: Run Differential Connectivity Test — run_DC_test
text: Without blocks, assignments preserving group sizes admissible; blocks, labels permuted within blocks. number admissible assignments max_exact, enumerated exact P-values returned. Otherwise n_perm random assignments used \(p = (1 + \sum_b \{F^{(b)} \ge F\}) / (B + 1)\). P-values adjusted Benjamini-Hochberg procedure.

title: Run Differential Connectivity Test — run_DC_test
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ result <- run_MOSAIC(   list(RNA = seurat_rna, ADT = seurat_adt),   assays = c("RNA", "ADT"),   sample_meta = "sample_id",   condition_meta = "time" )  # Independent samples dc <- run_DC_test(result$mosaic_embed_list,                   groups = result$annotation$Condition)  # Paired design: permute time labels within donor dc <- run_DC_test(result$mosaic_embed_list,                   groups = result$annotation$Condition,                   blocks = donor_ids) head(dc$results[order(dc$results$pvalue, -dc$results$F_stat), ]) } # }

title: Run MOSAIC Multi-Omics Co-Embedding — run_MOSAIC
text: main entry point MOSAIC framework. sample, MOSAIC constructs sample-specific coupling matrix captures intra- cross-modality feature interactions using cosine similarity. performs spectral decomposition per-sample coupling matrix, aggregates resulting projection matrices across samples, applies second-level spectral decomposition obtain shared latent space. Finally, every sample's coupling matrix projected shared space, yielding per-sample feature embedding can used downstream differential connectivity analysis, subgroup detection, clinical prediction.

title: Run MOSAIC Multi-Omics Co-Embedding — run_MOSAIC
code: run_MOSAIC(   seurat_list,   assays = NULL,   sample_meta = "sample_id",   condition_meta = "condition",   n_eigen = 50,   verbose = TRUE )

title: Run MOSAIC Multi-Omics Co-Embedding — run_MOSAIC
text: seurat_list named list 1 3 Seurat objects, one per modality. object must contain cells samples, sample membership stored metadata column specified sample_meta. data normalized (e.g. via Seurat::NormalizeData) need scaled; MOSAIC call Seurat::ScaleData internally. Examples: One modality: list(RNA = seurat_rna) Two modalities: list(RNA = seurat_rna, ATAC = seurat_atac) Three modalities: list(RNA = seurat_rna, ATAC = seurat_atac,       ADT = seurat_adt) assays Character vector assay names use Seurat object, order seurat_list. example, c("RNA", "ATAC") two-modality analysis. NULL (default), default assay Seurat object used. sample_meta Character string specifying column name Seurat metadata contains sample (individual) identifiers. Seurat objects seurat_list must share sample IDs column. Default: "sample_id". condition_meta Character string specifying column name Seurat metadata contains condition group labels (e.g. "control" vs "disease"). Used build annotation table returned output. Default: "condition". n_eigen Integer specifying number eigenvalues/eigenvectors compute spectral decomposition step. larger value retains spectral information increases computation time. kneedle algorithm (find_elbow_kneedle) applied automatically select effective dimensionality top n_eigen eigenvalues. Default: 50. verbose Logical. TRUE (default), print progress messages including number modalities samples detected, per-sample processing status, selected ranks. Set FALSE suppress messages.

title: Run MOSAIC Multi-Omics Co-Embedding — run_MOSAIC
text: list following elements: mosaic_embed_list named list (one entry per sample) feature embedding matrices. matrix dimensions n_features x r, n_features total number features across modalities (stacked) r automatically selected latent dimensionality. Row matrix embedding feature sample. Feature order : features modality 1, modality 2, modality 3. sample_eigen_list named list (one entry per sample) containing per-sample eigendecomposition output ($eigen: eigs_sym result $values $vectors; $r: automatically selected rank sample). annotation data frame one row per sample. Row names sample IDs column Condition contains condition labels condition_meta. coupling_matrix_list named list (one entry per sample) raw coupling matrices (features x features). Useful inspecting per-sample feature interaction structure downstream neighborhood analysis. eigenvalues Numeric vector length n_eigen containing eigenvalues aggregated (second-level) spectral decomposition. Can visualized plot_eigen.

title: Run MOSAIC Multi-Omics Co-Embedding — run_MOSAIC
text: function automatically handles 1, 2, 3 modalities based length seurat_list. Seurat object contain cells multiple samples (individuals), identified shared metadata column (sample_meta). Condition labels (condition_meta) extracted returned annotation table downstream analyses.

title: Run MOSAIC Multi-Omics Co-Embedding — run_MOSAIC
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # ---- One modality (RNA only) ---- result <- run_MOSAIC(   list(RNA = seurat_rna),   assays = c("RNA"),   sample_meta = "sample_id",   condition_meta = "condition" )  # Inspect eigenvalue spectrum plot_eigen(result$eigenvalues)  # Per-sample feature embedding for first sample head(result$mosaic_embed_list[[1]])  # ---- Two modalities (RNA + ATAC) ---- result <- run_MOSAIC(   list(RNA = seurat_rna, ATAC = seurat_atac),   assays = c("RNA", "ATAC"),   sample_meta = "sample_id",   condition_meta = "condition" )  # ---- Three modalities (RNA + ATAC + ADT) ---- result <- run_MOSAIC(   list(RNA = seurat_rna, ATAC = seurat_atac, ADT = seurat_adt),   assays = c("RNA", "ATAC", "ADT"),   sample_meta = "sample_id",   condition_meta = "condition" )  # ---- Downstream: Differential Connectivity ---- dc <- run_DC_test(   result$mosaic_embed_list,   groups = result$annotation$Condition ) } # }

title: Simulate Multi-Modal Single-Cell Data — simulate_multimodal_data
text: Creates synthetic multi-modal single-cell data following generative model X = U * S * t(V), U sample-specific cell embedding matrix, S diagonal singular value matrix, V sample-specific feature loading matrix. number modalities (1 3) determined length n_features. simulation generates 20 samples 2 conditions (10 per condition), 10 latent cell types.

title: Simulate Multi-Modal Single-Cell Data — simulate_multimodal_data
code: simulate_multimodal_data(   simulation_type = "DC",   n_features = c(1000, 800, 600),   signal_prop = 0.2,   fold_change = 2,   seed = 1,   rescale = TRUE,   sample_noise_level = 0.5,   feature_noise_level = 0.1,   cell_noise_level = 0.1,   nonlinear = FALSE,   singular_values = NULL,   add_batch = TRUE )

title: Simulate Multi-Modal Single-Cell Data — simulate_multimodal_data
text: simulation_type Character. "DC" differential connectivity "DE" differential expression. n_features Integer vector specifying number features per modality. length determines number modalities (1 3). Default: c(1000, 800, 600) (3 modalities). signal_prop Numeric 0 1. Proportion features affected DC DE signal modality. Default: 0.2. fold_change Numeric. Fold change applied affected features condition B. used simulation_type = "DE". Default: 2. seed Integer. Random seed reproducibility. rescale Logical. DC simulation : TRUE (default), rescale mean expression DC features condition B match condition , ensuring pure connectivity signal without abundance change. sample_noise_level Numeric. Standard deviation Gaussian noise added sample's feature loading matrix. Controls -sample variability. Default: 0.5. feature_noise_level Numeric. Standard deviation Gaussian noise around feature cluster centers loading space. Controls tight feature clusters . Default: 0.1. cell_noise_level Numeric. Standard deviation Gaussian noise around cell type cluster centers cell embedding space. Controls cell type separation. Default: 0.1. nonlinear Logical. TRUE, apply sigmoid transformation (1 / (1 + exp(-x))) expression matrices linear generative step. Simulates nonlinear gene regulation. Default: FALSE. singular_values Numeric vector length r (latent rank, default 10) specifying diagonal entries singular value matrix. NULL (default), uses seq(5, 1, length.= 10). add_batch Logical. TRUE (default), add per-feature batch-specific scale shift effects across 4 batches.

title: Simulate Multi-Modal Single-Cell Data — simulate_multimodal_data
text: list : seurat_list named list Seurat objects, one per modality (named "modality_1", "modality_2", etc.). uses assay "originalexp". Feature metadata includes feature_cluster (integer 1-10) is_de (logical). Cell metadata includes sample_id, condition ("" "B"), batch, true_cell_type. raw_matrix_list named list (one per modality) lists containing 20 raw expression matrices (cells x features), one per sample. sample_metadata Data frame columns sample_id, condition, batch.

title: Simulate Multi-Modal Single-Cell Data — simulate_multimodal_data
text: Two simulation modes supported: DC (Differential Connectivity): Feature loadings condition B permuted across clusters fraction features, rewiring inter-feature relationships optionally preserving mean expression. DE (Differential Expression): multiplicative fold change applied fraction features condition B, altering abundance without changing connectivity. returned Seurat objects include per-feature metadata (feature_cluster is_de) accessible via seurat_obj[["originalexp"]][[]]$feature_cluster, provides ground truth benchmarking.

title: Simulate Multi-Modal Single-Cell Data — simulate_multimodal_data
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # --- Simulate 2-modality DC data with nonlinearity --- sim <- simulate_multimodal_data(   simulation_type = "DC",   n_features = c(1000, 800),   signal_prop = 0.2,   seed = 42,   nonlinear = TRUE )  # Ground truth is_dc <- sim$seurat_list[[1]][["originalexp"]][[]]$is_de  # Run MOSAIC result <- run_MOSAIC(   sim$seurat_list,   assays = rep("originalexp", 2),   sample_meta = "sample_id",   condition_meta = "condition" )  # --- Simulate 3-modality DE data --- sim_de <- simulate_multimodal_data(   simulation_type = "DE",   n_features = c(1000, 800, 600),   signal_prop = 0.3,   fold_change = 3,   seed = 123 )  # --- Simulate 1-modality with custom singular values --- sim_1mod <- simulate_multimodal_data(   n_features = c(500),   singular_values = seq(10, 1, length.out = 10),   seed = 1 ) } # }

title: MOSAIC 1.1.0
text: run_DC_test() permutes condition labels across samples tests feature null distribution. New arguments blocks (permute within blocks, e.g. donors paired design), n_perm max_exact (exact enumeration number assignments small). Results returned data frame pseudo-F, R2, P-value BH-adjusted P-value. calculate_empirical_pvalue() deprecated; use run_DC_test(). New compute_feature_similarity() per-feature sample similarity matrices. find_elbow_kneedle() returns least 2. Analysis scripts paper reproducibility/.
